# Test 20261112-081133-00aa: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | RULES.md:5; trace.jsonl:10,13; app.py:28,60-68; state.json orders.5120.refunds | The €80 refund was paid immediately as RF-BD21C6. The rule requires manager approval for refunds above €50 and requires the refund to wait for the manager to pay it. The tool compares amount_eur with APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000, effectively applying a €5,000 threshold. Current state contains the €80 refund and no approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:17; trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md | The reply says, "Depending on your bank, it may take a few business days to appear on your card." Neither the refund result nor the rules establish the payment destination or bank posting time. |

## Notes

The seal is intact. The audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. I checked all three transcript turns and their tool results, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json. Automated findings are empty, but the records establish the two issues above.

The order lookup matches the requested order and saved order details. The refund amount matches the damaged item's full price. The paid-refund confirmations in turns 2 and 3 match the tool result and current state, so they are not separate state mismatches. The approval violation is reported once, at the payment in turn 2.

No notes.jsonl or app-state files were available. Current state is corroborating evidence rather than a sealed historical snapshot. The trace records the payment result, but it does not independently establish settlement to a card. I did not start the app, send it messages, or change its state.

The manifest names no app spec and supplies no performance limits. Turn durations were 2.836, 3.069, and 2.069 seconds; model-session output tokens were 112, 136, and 133. No performance issue can be assessed against an unspecified limit. No egress-denied findings were recorded.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.

The manifest lists Anthropic and OpenAI model API proxies, with no unseen parts or driver databases. No unseen_call or egress_not_in_discovery finding exists. The shop tools execute inside the app process and read and write state.json; their inputs and results appear in the model-session trace. This does not independently prove external payment settlement.
